Content:
In this lesson, we'll extend our understanding to include event complements.

The Venn diagram shown above represents two events [MATH: A] and [MATH: B] and the number of outcomes in each region of the sample space.

Given that every outcome is equally likely, find [MATH: P\left(A'\cap B\right).]
sections.readable_text:

The Venn diagram shown above represents two events [MATH: A] and [MATH: B] and the number of outcomes in each region of the sample space.

Given that every outcome is equally likely, find [MATH: P\left(A'\cap B\right).]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
To calculate the probability of an event using a Venn diagram, we count the number of outcomes in the region that represents the event, and divide by the total number of outcomes of the sample space [MATH: \mathcal S.]

In the Venn diagram, [MATH: A'\cap B] is represented by the area inside the circle [MATH: B] without the intersection between the circles (see the illustration below).

We count up the outcomes:

  • The number of outcomes in [MATH: A'\cap B] is [MATH: 7.]

  • The total number of outcomes in [MATH: \mathcal S] is [MATH: 9+3+7+11=30.]

So, we have [MATH: P\left(A'\cap B\right)=\dfrac{7}{30}.]

sections.normalized_html:
At an audition for the school band, there are [MATH: 35] volunteer students in total. Of the volunteers, [MATH: 20] students volunteer to play percussion, [MATH: 15] students volunteer to play a wind instrument, and [MATH: 3] students volunteer for both percussion and wind instruments.

Represent the corresponding sample space using a Venn diagram. If we randomly select a student among the [MATH: 35] students, what is the probability that they volunteered for neither percussion nor wind instruments? Give your answers to [MATH: 2] decimal places.
sections.readable_text:
At an audition for the school band, there are [MATH: 35] volunteer students in total. Of the volunteers, [MATH: 20] students volunteer to play percussion, [MATH: 15] students volunteer to play a wind instrument, and [MATH: 3] students volunteer for both percussion and wind instruments.

Represent the corresponding sample space using a Venn diagram. If we randomly select a student among the [MATH: 35] students, what is the probability that they volunteered for neither percussion nor wind instruments? Give your answers to [MATH: 2] decimal places.

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Let us call [MATH: A] the event "The student volunteers to play percussion" and [MATH: B] the event "The student volunteers to play a wind instrument."

Note that there are [MATH: 3] students who volunteer for both percussion and wind instruments. We draw two overlapping circles representing the events [MATH: A] and [MATH: B] and write the number [MATH: 3] where the circles overlap.

  • The number of students who volunteer for percussion only is [MATH: 20 - 3 = 17,] so we write the number [MATH: 17] in the part of circle [MATH: A] that does not overlap with circle [MATH: B.]

  • The number of students who volunteer for wind instruments only is [MATH: 15 - 3 = 12,] so we write the number [MATH: 12] in the part of the circle [MATH: B] that does not overlap with circle [MATH: A.]

The total number of students who volunteered for percussion or wind instruments is [MATH: 3 + 17 + 12 = 32,] and there are [MATH: 35] students in total, so the number of remaining students is [MATH: 35 - 32 = 3.]

To represent these [MATH: 3] students who did not volunteer for wind instruments or percussion, we write the number [MATH: 3] outside of the circles [MATH: A] and [MATH: B.]

Therefore, our final Venn diagram looks as shown below:

The shaded part of the Venn diagram corresponds to students who volunteered neither for percussion nor wind instruments. The probability that a randomly selected student is from this group is given by

[MATH: P(A'\cap B')=\dfrac{3}{35} \approx 0.09,] rounded to [MATH: 2] decimal places.

so we write the number [MATH: 17] in the part of circle [MATH: A] that does not overlap with circle [MATH: B.]

[IMG: /graphics/08bbe881a4e8d29179e0941ad1fad0ef]

- The number of students who volunteer for wind instruments only is
[MATH: 15 - 3 = 12,]

[IMG: /graphics/fc896e06c135813ee1d98ada8ed243df]

[MATH: 3 + 17 + 12 = 32,]
